name: Tan-extender moisturizer
lead: Tan-extender moisturizers are hydrating lotions marketed to prolong the colour of a sunless (self) tan. Self-tan colour from dihydroxyacetone (DHA) sits in the dead outer layer of skin and is described as fading over roughly 3 to 10 days as that layer is shed.[1] Extender products are positioned as slowing that fade, and some contain small amounts of DHA to top up colour.
No published trial has measured whether tan-extender moisturizers lengthen the life of a self-tan. The one indexed medical report concerns an allergic reaction to an ingredient.

paras: Sunless tans fade as the skin cell layer containing the colour is shed, a process lasting about 3 to 10 days.[1] Hydrating products are marketed on the idea that supple skin sheds more slowly, though no published study tested this for these products.

A 2024 case report in Contact Dermatitis described protein contact dermatitis to a tan-extender lotion, with the authors assessing pumpkin seed oil (Luffa cylindrica seed oil) as the probable cause.[2] It is a single report and does not give a rate of reactions.

refs.title: Protein contact dermatitis to a tan-extender lotion: Imputability of pumpkin seed oil (Luffa cylindrica seed oil)

card.summary: Hydrating lotion sold to stretch out a self-tan; the claim is untested.
card.note: Allergic reaction to one such lotion has been reported.

quick.overview:
A tan-extender is a moisturizer marketed to make a self-tan last longer, sometimes with a little added DHA.

No trial has tested whether it extends tan life.
quick.mechanism: Self-tan colour sits in the dead outer skin layer and fades over about 3 to 10 days as it sheds.[1] Extenders are marketed as slowing this by hydrating the skin.
quick.risks: A 2024 case report described protein contact dermatitis to one tan-extender lotion, attributed to pumpkin seed oil.[2]
